title: API Fault Quick Scripts for Oncall
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, on-call centric set of scripts and heuristics for fast mitigation of common API degradations: request timeouts, 429s (rate limiting), streaming stalls/partial responses, and sustained elevated error rates (5xx). The goal is to provide quick, low-risk actions that restore customer-visible behavior while the deeper investigation happens.

Scope and assumptions:
- Targets Redwood API endpoints (hosted + dedicated routing layer).
- Applies to both synchronous generation endpoints and streaming responses.
- Assumes SLO/alerting is already firing and basic dashboards are available (latency by route, error budget burn, token throughput).
- This is operator shorthand — expand into a full postmortem if the incident > 30m or customer impact is > critical.

Quick triage checklist (first 5 minutes):
1) Confirm alert source and scope: which route/model/region? Copy alert details to incident channel (#sre-oncall).
2) Check global health dashboards: 95th/99th latency, 5xx rate, 429 rate, streaming error rate.
3) Identify blast radius: a single route? all routes? single region? single cluster?
4) If latency spike + traffic spike: enable protective throttles. If errors spike: consider immediate fallback to lower-capacity model variant.
5) Announce: "Investigating: [high-level symptom]. Triage lead: @<name>. ETA 15m for next update."

Common investigative queries (Prometheus/Datadog examples) - copy/paste:
- 1m 99p latency for route X: 
  query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=\"/v1/generate\"}[2m])) by (le))
- 5xx rate: 
  query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\",route=\"/v1/*\"}[1m])) by (route,region)
- 429 rate: 
  query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=\"429\",route=~\"/v1/.*\"}[1m])) by (route)
- Streaming: count of stream disconnects / minute: custom_metric.stream_disconnect_count / 1m

Scenario A: Timeouts / Latency spikes
Signals:
- 95p/99p latency jump, tail increases, clients seeing 504 or socket timeouts.
Immediate mitigations (low risk):
- Reduce per-request max_tokens and/or reduce top_p/top_k for problematic route via runtime config to shrink inference time. Command snippet: edit route config in Console -> temporary concurrency limit / token cap.
- Increase autoscaler target for serving pool for the route (if on Dedicated): kubectl -n serving patch hpa <hpa-name> --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":<bump>}}' (work with infra on quota).
- Enable degraded-mode routing: route traffic to a quantized or smaller model variant (route -> fallback_model: small-qa-quant). This reduces latency at the cost of quality.
- Short-term enqueue/backpressure: toggle rate-limiter to shift bursts to queue with bounded latency (Console toggle: rate-limit->burst-window 10s).
When to escalate:
- If tail latency remains > SLO after applying degraded-mode and scaling for 10 minutes, escalate to platform-eng and infra. Open incident ticket SRE-1423 (example).

Scenario B: 429s (rate-limit responses)
Signals:
- Sudden rise in 429 counts for a route, often with stable upstream capacity utilization.
Immediate mitigations (steps ordered by risk):
- Verify global rate-limit config change or release (recent PRs). Check recent deploys: GitHub Actions -> last 30m.
- Temporarily relax per-key or per-route rate limit thresholds. Query token bucket metrics to see burst patterns.
- Turn on tenant-level soft-fallback: allow a small percentage of requests to bypass strict throttling for high-SLA keys (console -> policies -> exceptions).
- If 429s are due to downstream dependency (e.g., model worker queue full), reduce concurrency by enabling slower but more reliable path (cache-hit path).
Fast checks:
- Check redis/broker queue lengths: redis-cli LLEN inference:queue:<route>
- Check token issuance logs for sudden client misbehavior (abusive retry storms).

Scenario C: Degraded streaming (partial frames, long pauses, truncated outputs)
Signals:
- Clients report partial chunks or streams stopping mid-response, stream disconnect and reconnect logs rising.
Immediate mitigations:
- If streaming proxy is overloaded, switch streams to chunked-polling fallback for affected clients (Console toggle: streaming->fallback-polling).
- Increase streaming buffer / keepalive timeouts at the gateway temporarily.
- If KV-cache pressure suspected, flush or shrink cache entries for offending model to free memory: (ops command: flushkvcache --model small-llama-13b --confirm).
- Activate stream-graceful-fallback: continue sending best-effort cached prefix and then close with a short explanation token (implemented as response meta in runtime).
When to escalate:
- If disconnects persist after proxy tuning and cache adjustments for 10m, involve serving-runtime oncall to inspect kernel saturation and mem traces.

Scenario D: Elevated error rates (5xx)
Signals:
- Spike in 500/502/503 across one or many routes.
Immediate mitigations:
- Roll back recent routing or configuration changes (most common cause). Identify PRs merged in last 30m.
- Circuit-break: flip the per-route CB to open for a short window to protect downstream systems. (Console: route -> circuit-break -> open)
- Enable fallback runner: route to a statically served response (e.g., cached best-effort) for non-critical routes while keeping critical routes alive.
- If the issue stems from model workers OOM/crash loops: scale down batch_size and restart small pool of workers for warm-up.

Communication templates (short):
- First update (10m): "Investigating increased [timeouts/429s/streaming failures/5xx] impacting /v1/* in eu-west. Limited blast radius; applying protective measures. Next update in 15m. SRE lead: @AvaM."
- Service degraded (customer-facing): "We're seeing degraded response times for API generation. We're applying throttles and fallbacks to stabilize. We'll update within 30 minutes. Contact support@redwood if urgent."

Operator command cheat-sheet (examples):
- Check recent deploys: gh api repos/redwood-inference/platform/actions/runs --jq '.workflow_runs[0:5] | .[] | {id,name,status,created_at}'
- Inspect worker logs (k8s): kubectl -n serving logs deployment/infer-worker --tail=200 --selector=app=infer-worker
- Bump pool replicas: kubectl -n serving scale deployment/infer-pool-<route> --replicas=6
- Toggle route fallback via API: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.api/redwood/routes/<route>/toggle_fallback -d '{"fallback":"small-quant"}'

Post-incident quick actions (first 48 hours):
- Capture timeline with exact timestamps and config changes.
- Identify the root cause and any contributing factors: deploys, traffic anomalies, changed thresholds.
- Run synthetic checks against the affected route with production-like payloads to validate fix (script: tests/synthetic/load_run.sh).
- Add a postmortem owner and publish within 72 hours.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (living section):
- Add automated quick-toggle for streaming->polling fallback (dev work item).
- Define explicit per-route degraded-mode quality thresholds and SLIs to auto-trigger model-fallbacks.
- Add a discovery query to map customer keys to rate-limit buckets (helps with selective exceptions).

Notes to self / operator tips (informal):
- When in doubt, reduce quality (smaller model / quantized variant) rather than keep clients blocked. The perceived availability wins over occasional lower-quality outputs.
- Keep a short list of high-SLA keys we never throttle without explicit approval. Store as secrets in vault and surface in Console.
- Use short, explicit updates in incident channel; avoid speculation. Save analysis for the postmortem doc.

References and follow-ups:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.internal/sre/api-responses-degradation-playbook (draft)
- Jira: SRE-1423 (investigate recent autoscaler change)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/987 (rate-limit refactor)

End of operator pocket script. Keep this doc lean — expand into a full runbook when patterns repeat or when we push run-time toggles into the Console UI.
